t_008fc7e9.title: T1 coder: scaffold repo + backend API/DB + tests
t_008fc7e9.body:
You are the sole implementation writer for the Coffee Notes project. Read `docs/SPEC.md` (binding technical contract), `docs/BRIEF.md` (owner requirements) and `docs/ASSUMPTIONS.md` first. Use the team-contract, team-quality and team-verify skills.

REPOSITORY: /home/hermes/workspace/coffee-notes (workspace_path is already set). Branch `main`, baseline commit `48da0af` (docs + vendored fonts only). Do not rewrite or delete docs/, evidence/ or scripts/fetch-fonts.py. Do not touch anything outside this repository.

DELIVERABLE (T1 = backend only, frontend is T2): a working server + database + API + tests + operational doc, serving a placeholder static page so the app can be started end to end.

1. `package.json` — name `coffee-notes`, `"type":"module"`, `"engines":{"node":">=22"}`, NO runtime dependencies, scripts exactly per SPEC §6 (`start`, `dev`, `test`, `seed`, `check`).
2. `server/schema.sql`, `server/db.js` — SQLite via `node:sqlite` `DatabaseSync`, `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` and `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, linear idempotent migrations recorded in `schema_migrations`, prepared statements, all queries in this module. Data model exactly as SPEC §4 including the partial unique index on the single default grinder and the `grinder_name` snapshot column.
3. `server/router.js` + `server/index.js` — `node:http` server bound to `127.0.0.1`, port/config per SPEC §3, small method+path router, JSON body parsing with a size limit (e.g. 256 KB) and clear 400 on malformed JSON, uniform error envelope per SPEC §7, 404 for unknown routes, 405 where a known path is called with a wrong method, static file serving with correct MIME types and no path traversal (reject `..` after decoding). Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM (close server + DB). Startup log line with resolved host/port/db path.
4. `server/api.js` — every route in SPEC §7 with the validation rules exactly as written: `brewed_at` format + real calendar validity, numeric ranges, field-level error messages, `grinder_name` snapshot resolution, duplicate/blank grinder handling (409/400), single-default invariant, `DELETE` of a grinder promoting the oldest remaining (or null), `newest first` ordering, `q`/`grinder`/`limit` query handling. `grinder_id` referencing a missing grinder must be a 400 field error, and a deleted grinder must leave the note readable with its snapshot name.
5. `server/seed.js` — 5 realistic demo notes + 2 demo grinders (only when no grinder exists), all with `is_demo=1`; CLI `node server/seed.js --demo`; `DELETE /api/demo` removes `is_demo=1` rows only.
6. `test/db.test.js` and `test/api.test.js` — `node:test`, temp DB file inside the process scratch dir (never the repo `data/`), ephemeral port. Cover: create/read/update/delete note; validation failures (bad `brewed_at` e.g. `2026-02-30T10:00`, `2026-10-11T25:00`, non-numeric/negative grind size, dose/water out of range); blank and duplicate grinder names; setting default clears the previous one; deleting the default promotes another; deleting a grinder keeps its notes with the snapshot name and null `grinder_id`; demo seed then clear leaves user notes intact; `q` filter and ordering newest first; malformed JSON; unknown route; persistence across a closed-and-reopened database handle (simulating process restart).
7. `scripts/check.js` — the `npm run check` build check described in SPEC §6. It must pass on your code.
8. `public/index.html` — minimal placeholder (project name, the design tokens from SPEC §5, a link to `public/fonts/dm-sans.css`, text stating the UI lands in the next task and the API is live). Keep it tiny; do not build the real UI.
9. `docs/OPERATIONS.md` — start/stop, URL, DB path, backup command, Windows SSH tunnel line, note that the app process is separate from Hermes. Reference `docs/SPEC.md` for the API instead of duplicating it; if you document routes, keep a short table only.
10. `evidence/receipts/T1-coder.md` — receipt per the team-verify skill: task id, candidate SHA, exact commands run, exit codes, observed behaviour, limitations, and confirmation that `npm test` and `npm run check` pass and the server answered `GET /api/health` plus a real note round-trip through `curl`.

BOUNDS: local-only completion. No GitHub push (the coordinator publishes), no LAN/public binding, no new npm runtime dependency, no frameworks, no TypeScript build step, no Docker, no unrelated files or refactors. Do not modify `docs/SPEC.md`; if the spec is genuinely unworkable, note it in the receipt and in a Kanban comment instead of silently diverging.

VERIFY BEFORE HANDING OFF: `npm run check`, `npm test`, then start the server and run a real curl round-trip (create grinder → create note → list → delete note) against the running process. Then commit with `git -c user.name=DesBots -c user.email=des.agent.bot@gmail.com commit` and report the candidate SHA, changed files and the exact command output summary. A source change after your receipt invalidates it, so commit last.

t_465f2318.title: T2 coder: frontend core — design system, history sidebar, detail and editor
t_465f2318.body:
You are the sole implementation writer for the Coffee Notes frontend, second implementation card. Read `docs/SPEC.md` — §5 (design tokens), §7 (API) and §8 (frontend behaviour) are binding — plus `docs/BRIEF.md` and `docs/ASSUMPTIONS.md`. Use the team-contract, team-quality and team-verify skills. This card is gated on the backend card `t_008fc7e9`; start from its candidate commit and read its receipt in `evidence/receipts/`.

SCOPE: the complete core UI. Replace the `public/index.html` placeholder and build `public/styles.css` + ES modules under `public/js/`. Do NOT modify `server/`, `test/`, `docs/BRIEF.md` or `docs/SPEC.md`. If the backend is missing something you genuinely need, note it in a Kanban comment and work around it client-side — do not silently change the API contract.

DELIVERABLE:
1. Warm design system in `public/styles.css` using the exact tokens in SPEC §5: cream `#F7F0E6` page, off-white surfaces, espresso/brown/tan accents, rounded cards (14px) and controls (10px), restrained 1px `--line` borders, subtle layered shadows, generous purposeful spacing. Typography via `@font-face` from `public/fonts/dm-sans.css` with the system fallback stack. No CSS framework, no preprocessor, no inline `<style>` blocks beyond nothing — one stylesheet. Keep it organised with short section comments.
2. App shell: fixed left history sidebar (320–360px) + spacious detail/editor pane filling the rest, on cream with card surfaces. Header shows the app name and a `New note` button.
3. History sidebar: notes newest first, each row showing date+time, grinder name, bean name (or `—`), and grind size when set; unmistakable selected state (tinted background + 3px tan/brown left accent + bold title + `aria-current="true"`). Clicking a row selects that note and renders it in the pane.
4. Detail view: full note rendering with a labelled field list (brew date/time, grinder, grind size, dose/water, `Ratio 1:16.0` when both are present, bean name/origin/roast, tasting notes with `white-space: pre-wrap`), plus `Edit` and `Delete` actions in the pane header.
5. Editor: same pane, entered by `New note` or `Edit`. Labelled inputs bound with `for`/`id`, `datetime-local` for brew date/time, number inputs for grind size/dose/water, select for grinder (options from `GET /api/grinders`, default preselected), select for roast level (unset/light/medium/dark), textarea for tasting notes. Inline field errors under the offending input with `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby` pointing at the error node. `Save` shows a `Saving…` disabled state while in flight and on success returns to the detail view with a success toast. `Cancel` returns to detail.
6. New-note defaults: `brewed_at` = current local date/time as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` computed from local clock parts (never `toISOString()`), grinder = the default grinder from `GET /api/grinders`. If no grinders exist, show an inline hint pointing at Settings and allow saving with a typed grinder name (the API accepts `grinder_name` without `grinder_id`).
7. Cancelling a brand-new note must not call the API and must not leave an empty row anywhere. Editing then cancelling reverts to the stored version.
8. Unsaved-changes protection: `beforeunload` prompt while dirty; in-app navigation (selecting another note, opening settings, `New note` while dirty) asks for confirmation first; `Esc` in a dirty editor asks before discarding.
9. Delete: modal confirmation dialog naming the note's date and grinder (`Delete note` is the destructive label), focus trapped, `Esc` cancels. Deletes only after confirmation.
10. States: loading skeletons for sidebar and pane; empty state when there are no notes at all (friendly, specific copy + `New note` button); a distinct filtered/no-results empty state; API-failure banner with a `Retry` button and a plain-language message (never a raw stack trace); success toast for save/delete. Errors must never leave the UI stuck in a spinner.
11. Basics for later cards but wired now: a settings entry point and a search input are allowed as long as they are honest (search may filter the loaded list client-side against `GET /api/notes?q=`). Demo/sample-data affordances, the full settings dialog, the mobile drawer, the `Ctrl/Cmd+N` shortcut and the accessibility sweep belong to card T3 — do not half-build them here.
12. All network access via `fetch` to the same origin `/api/...`. No `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` holding note data (the DB is the only store). No external CDN, no analytics, no web fonts fetched over the network.

QUALITY BAR: this is a portfolio-quality local app for one person — hierarchy, alignment and spacing must look deliberate, not like a bootstrap demo. Avoid clutter, excessive ornament, marketing sections and placeholder copy.

VERIFY BEFORE HANDING OFF (all must actually run):
- `npm test` still passes and `npm run check` passes (extend `scripts/check.js` only if the new files require it, e.g. new directory entries).
- Start the server, then use `curl` to confirm the API round-trip still works, and load `http://127.0.0.1:4317/` to confirm the page and its JS/CSS/font requests all return 200 (check the server log for 404s).
- Optional but encouraged browser smoke check: the coordinator's Playwright tooling lives outside this repo at `/home/hermes/workspace/tools/ui-evidence` (playwright + Chromium already installed). You may run a throwaway script from that directory against your running server; do not commit it here and do not install anything into this repo. If it is unavailable, say so — do not claim a browser check you did not run.
- Write `evidence/receipts/T2-coder.md`: task id, candidate SHA, exact commands, exit codes, observed behaviour, limitations, and which of the six brief acceptance checks you exercised versus left to the tester.
- Commit last with `git -c user.name=DesBots -c user.email=des.agent.bot@gmail.com commit`, then report the candidate SHA and changed files in your Kanban completion.

BOUNDS: local-only completion, no push, no new runtime dependency, no build step, no Docker, no unrelated files. Do not touch `server/`, other cards' receipts, `docs/BRIEF.md`, `docs/SPEC.md` or `docs/ASSUMPTIONS.md`.

t_24b95f3b.title: T3 coder: settings, search, sample data, mobile drawer, accessibility polish
t_24b95f3b.body:
You are the sole implementation writer for the Coffee Notes frontend completion card. Read `docs/SPEC.md` §5, §7 and §8 (binding), `docs/BRIEF.md` and `docs/ASSUMPTIONS.md`. Use team-contract, team-quality and team-verify. Gated on `t_465f2318` (frontend core); start from its candidate commit and read `evidence/receipts/T2-coder.md` for what it deliberately left out.

SCOPE: finish and polish the frontend. Touch only `public/**` (plus `scripts/check.js` if the file list needs updating). Do NOT rewrite the core that works, do not modify `server/`, `test/`, or the docs.

DELIVERABLE:
1. **Grinder settings** (dialog on desktop ≥820px, full-height sheet on mobile): list every grinder with its note count from `GET /api/grinders`; add form (`Add grinder`, inline error under the input for blank or duplicate names — duplicate must show the server's 409 message and must not create a row); rename; `Make default` with a clear single-default indicator (badge/radio-like control); `Remove` with a confirmation that explicitly says historical notes keep their grinder name; after removing the default the app must reflect the promoted default (or "no grinders yet"). All actions update the list without a full page reload, and failures show a message instead of silently doing nothing.
2. **Search/filter** in the sidebar: text query against `GET /api/notes?q=` (debounced ~200ms, cancel stale responses so a slow response cannot overwrite a newer one), a `Clear` affordance, and a distinct "no notes match" empty state that is different from the "no notes at all" state.
3. **Demo/sample data**: a clearly labelled `Load sample notes` action (calls `POST /api/demo/seed`) available from the empty state and from Settings, plus `Remove sample notes` (`DELETE /api/demo`). Sample rows must be visually marked as samples (e.g. a `Sample` chip) and never mixed in silently with user notes. Loading samples twice must not duplicate them.
4. **Mobile (≤820px)**: sidebar becomes a drawer opened by a `Notes` button in the header, with a dimmed backdrop, body scroll lock, focus trap, `Esc` and backdrop-click close, `aria-modal="true"`, and background content marked `aria-hidden`. Selecting a note closes the drawer. Single-column forms, controls ≥44px tall, no horizontal overflow at 360px width.
5. **Keyboard**: `Ctrl/Cmd+N` starts a new note, ignored when focus is in an input/textarea/select/contenteditable or a dialog is open, and it must not hijack the browser when it cannot be handled; `Esc` closes dialogs/drawer before anything else. Visible `:focus-visible` ring (2px brown, 2px offset) everywhere, logical tab order, and a skip-to-content link if the layout benefits.
6. **Accessibility and state audit** across the app: every control labelled, toasts in an `aria-live="polite"` region, dialog focus/return-focus handled, no colour-only meaning, contrast ≥4.5:1 for body text on the cream/espresso palette, and the five states (loading, empty, validation, API-error, success) verifiably reachable. Fix what is missing in the core card rather than duplicating it.
7. Optional: a short `docs/KEYBOARD.md` (≤30 lines) listing the shortcuts and the accessibility behaviours you implemented. Do not turn it into a marketing page.

VERIFY BEFORE HANDING OFF (all must actually run):
- `npm run check` and `npm test` pass (they must not regress).
- Manual/real-browser pass: run the server and exercise, at minimum, add-grinder → make default → new note → save → refresh → edit → cancel → delete-with-confirm, plus a mobile-viewport check at 390×844 and a 360px overflow check. The coordinator's Playwright tooling is at `/home/hermes/workspace/tools/ui-evidence` (Chromium installed, system libs present) — you may run throwaway scripts from that directory. Report exactly which checks you ran and which you could not.
- `evidence/receipts/T3-coder.md`: task id, candidate SHA, commands, exit codes, observed behaviour, what you verified in a real browser, and limitations.
- Commit last with `git -c user.name=DesBots -c user.email=des.agent.bot@gmail.com commit`, and report the candidate SHA in your completion.

BOUNDS: local-only, no push, no new runtime dependency, no build step, no frameworks, no CDN, no unrelated features (no brew timers, statistics, charts, cloud sync, notifications). Keep the app one straightforward repository with simple commands.

t_5d0de379.title: T4 tester: independent acceptance verification of the running app
t_5d0de379.body:
You are the independent tester for the Coffee Notes app. Use the team-contract, team-quality, team-verify and team-debug skills. Gated on `t_24b95f3b` (frontend completion); start from that candidate commit. Read `docs/SPEC.md` and `docs/BRIEF.md` — the brief's "Verification and visual evidence" section defines acceptance.

YOU DO NOT PATCH CODE. You reproduce behaviour against the real running app and report evidence. Any source change makes your receipt stale. If you find a defect, record the exact reproduction, the observed result, the expected result and any logs, then mark the card failed in your completion summary and comment — the coordinator will raise a narrow fix card.

SETUP: `cd /home/hermes/workspace/coffee-notes`, use a **copy** of the repository (e.g. `cp -a` to `/home/hermes/.hermes/cache/scratch/t4-verify`) or at minimum a temp `COFFEE_NOTES_DB` path so your destructive delete checks never touch the real `data/coffee-notes.db`. Record the candidate SHA (`git rev-parse HEAD`) before and after your run; if it changes, re-verify.

RUN THESE (record exact commands, exit codes and observed output into `evidence/receipts/T4-tester.md`):
1. `npm run check` and `npm test` — run them yourself; do not trust the coder's receipt.
2. Start the app (`COFFEE_NOTES_PORT=4318 npm start` with a temp DB) and confirm `GET /api/health` answers and the process binds 127.0.0.1 only (check with `ss -ltnp` that it is not listening on 0.0.0.0).

ACCEPTANCE CHECKS (each needs a PASS/FAIL verdict with the evidence that produced it):
1. Add a grinder, make it the default, create a note using it — verify via API response and via the UI that the default is preselected for the new note.
2. View a note, edit it, cancel an unsaved new note (confirm no row was created — count notes before/after), and delete a note through the confirmation dialog (and confirm the row is gone).
3. Persistence: create notes/settings, refresh the browser page, then kill the server process and start it again — the notes and default grinder must still be there. Browser storage must not be the store: verify a fresh browser context (no storage state) still shows the data.
4. Remove a grinder preset that historical notes use; those notes must survive with their grinder name still displayed and no crash/500.
5. Invalid input: `2026-02-30T10:00`, `2026-10-11T25:00`, negative/absurd grind size and dose/water values → clear field-level feedback in the UI and 400 with `fields` in the API. API-failure path: make the API fail (e.g. stop the server, or request a bad id like `/api/notes/999999`) and confirm the UI shows a useful error with a retry, never a stuck spinner or a raw stack trace.
6. Layout: desktop 1440×900 and mobile 390×844 and 360×844 — no horizontal overflow (`document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth + 1`), drawer opens/closes with backdrop and `Esc`, all visible controls usable and ≥44px tall on mobile, focus ring visible, dialog focus trapped.

BROWSER TOOLING: Playwright + Chromium are installed outside the app repo at `/home/hermes/workspace/tools/ui-evidence` (system libs installed). Run throwaway scripts from that directory (`node script.mjs`) against your test instance; do NOT install anything into the app repo and do not add playwright to the app's package.json. Save raw browser screenshots/logs you rely on under `evidence/test/` (not `evidence/ui/`, which the coordinator owns for final showcase captures).

ALSO CHECK: the six UI states are genuinely reachable (loading, empty, validation, API-error, success, and a distinct filtered-empty), `Ctrl/Cmd+N` does not fire while typing in an input, and the sample/demo notes are clearly marked and separable from user notes.

EVIDENCE: `evidence/receipts/T4-tester.md` — 150–300 words plus a per-check verdict table, exact commands, exit codes, observed behaviour, limitations, and any check you could not run (a skipped check is never a pass). Raw logs may go to `evidence/test/`. Do not run `git commit` (report the SHA you tested); do not modify source, `docs/`, or another card's receipt.

BUDGET: stop after two unsuccessful attempts at the same failure cause — preserve the evidence and report the blocker instead of looping.

t_8fc61842.title: T5 reviewer: independent diff review and complexity assessment
t_8fc61842.body: You are the independent reviewer for the Coffee Notes app. Use the team-contract, team-quality, team-verify and team-review skills. Gated on `t_5d0de379` (tester); read the tester receipt and the two coder receipts first (`evidence/receipts/`), plus `docs/SPEC.md` and `docs/BRIEF.md`. YOU DO NOT PATCH CODE. You inspect the actual diff and the actual repository state, then report defects, risks and needless complexity with file:line references. Do not rewrite the implementation; return findings so the coordinator can raise a narrow fix card. START: `cd /home/hermes/workspace/coffee-notes`, record `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status` (a dirty tree means the candidate is not what the receipts describe — report it). The implementation diff to review is `a7c465d..HEAD` (baseline docs commit through the final candidate). Read the code, not just the receipts. t_ea659a25.title: T3b coder: fix stale grinder state in Settings (add/rename/make-default never refresh)
t_ea659a25.body:
Narrow fix card for the Coffee Notes frontend. Use team-quality and team-verify. Read `docs/SPEC.md` §8 first. Repository: `/home/hermes/workspace/coffee-notes`, branch `main`, start from the current HEAD (`7f39dc4`, i.e. T3's candidate `b69a65e` plus its receipt).

## Confirmed defect (found and reproduced by the coordinator)
**Grinder settings never reflect changes made while its dialog is open.**

Root cause, in `public/app.js` `showSettings()` (around lines 410–445): the `actions` object refreshes application state for `remove` (calls `await loadGrinders()`), `seed` and `clearDemo`, but **`add`, `rename` and `makeDefault` only perform the API call and never call `loadGrinders()`**. `createSettings` re-reads the list through `snapshot()` → `settingsSnapshot()` → `state.grinders`, which is therefore stale, so `render()` redraws the same old list. `public/js/settings.js`'s own docstring claims "the visible list cannot drift from the server" — it currently can.

Observed (fresh DB, Playwright/Chromium, desktop 1440×900):
- Open Settings with 0 presets → add "Alpha Grinder" and "Beta Grinder": the status line says `Alpha Grinder added.` / `Beta Grinder added.` and `GET /api/grinders` returns both rows, but the dialog shows **0 rows** — still 0 rows 3 s and 6 s later, and the empty-state message stays. The presets are invisible and unusable.
- Open Settings when presets already exist, then click `Make default` on a non-default preset: `GET /api/grinders` shows the new `is_default`, but the `Default` badge stays on the old row.
- Same staleness class for `rename` and for the editor/sidebar grinder list after an add.

## Required change
Make every grinder mutation refresh the application's grinder state before the dialog re-renders, exactly the way `remove` already does:
- `add`: `const payload = await api.createGrinder(name); await loadGrinders(); return payload.grinder;`
- `rename`: rename, then `await loadGrinders()`, return the grinder.
- `makeDefault`: set the default, then `await loadGrinders()`, return the grinder.
Keep the existing `remove`/`seed`/`clearDemo` behaviour. Do not restructure `createSettings`, do not change the API, `server/`, `test/`, docs, or the other receipts. Prefer the smallest diff that makes the state refresh correct; if a single shared helper removes three near-identical blocks, that is acceptable and preferable to triplication.

## Verify before handing off (keep this tight)
1. `npm run check` and `npm test` both still pass.
2. Real-browser repro, from an **empty database** (`COFFEE_NOTES_DB` in the process scratch dir, a non-default port): open Settings → add two grinders → both rows appear with the first one carrying `Default` → click `Make default` on the second → the badge moves to it → rename a grinder and see the new name → remove one and see it go, with its note count and any notes intact.
   The coordinator's tooling is at `/home/hermes/workspace/tools/ui-evidence` (Playwright + Chromium already installed). `bash run-sweep.sh <port>` runs a broader 30-check acceptance sweep against a fresh DB — use it if you like, but do not add it or playwright to this repository.
3. Do NOT perform a broad regression sweep or investigate unrelated areas — the tester card `t_5d0de379` owns full acceptance verification and the reviewer card `t_5d0de379`'s successor owns the code review.

## Delivery
- Commit early rather than late: commit the fix as soon as checks pass, with `git -c user.name=DesBots -c user.email=des.agent.bot@gmail.com commit`.
- Write `evidence/receipts/T3b-coder.md` (≤200 words): task id, candidate SHA, the exact commands, exit codes, the observed before/after behaviour in a real browser, limitations.
- Complete the card with the candidate SHA. Local-only: no push, no new dependency, no build step.

BUDGET: this is a small, precisely located fix. Stop after two unsuccessful attempts at the same symptom, preserve the evidence and report the blocker rather than looping.

t_22570dcc.title: T6 coder: fix detail-load error feedback and dialog focus traps
t_22570dcc.body:
Narrow fix card for three confirmed defects in the Coffee Notes frontend. Use team-quality and team-verify. Read `docs/SPEC.md` §8 (states, dialogs, accessibility) first. Repository: `/home/hermes/workspace/coffee-notes`, branch `main`, start from the current HEAD. Do NOT touch `server/`, `test/`, `docs/`, or other cards' receipts; keep the diff small and targeted.

All three were reproduced by the coordinator with Playwright/Chromium in `public/`-only code paths (probe output on request; tooling lives in `/home/hermes/workspace/tools/ui-evidence`, run throwaway scripts from there and never commit them or playwright into this repo).

## Defect 1 — a failed single-note load gives the user nothing (acceptance check #5)
Repro: seed one note, open the app, then `page.route('**/api/notes/*', r => r.abort())` and click a history row.
Observed: `GET /api/notes/:id` fails, and afterwards `#banner` is `hidden` with empty text and there is **no Retry button anywhere** in the document (`retryButtons=0`). The pane keeps showing the previous note as if nothing happened.
Required: a failed detail/editor load must surface the same visible banner + `Retry` affordance the failed *list* load already uses, with a plain-language message, and `Retry` must succeed once the API is reachable again (reload the selected note and render it). The failure must not leave the pane showing stale content as if it were current.

## Defect 2 — the delete confirmation dialog does not take or trap focus
Repro: click a history row, click `Delete`, then press `Tab` repeatedly and inspect `document.activeElement`.
Observed: on open, focus is on `<body>` (the dialog never takes focus), and the containment sequence alternates — every second `Tab` lands outside the dialog (`truefalsetruefalse…`).
Required: on open, move focus into the confirmation dialog; the initial focus should be the non-destructive choice (`Keep note`), `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` must cycle only through the dialog's controls, `Esc` still cancels, and focus returns to the `Delete` button that opened it when the dialog closes.

## Defect 3 — the settings dialog focus trap leaks
Repro: open `Settings`, press `Tab` twelve times then `Shift+Tab` four times, recording `dialog[open].contains(document.activeElement)` each time.
Observed: containment is `truetruetruetruetruetruefalse…` — focus escapes the dialog after roughly six tabs (the dialog body is re-rendered after actions, so a trap that resolves its focusable list once, or that ignores buttons while they are disabled, goes stale).
Required: focus stays inside `dialog[open]` for any number of tab presses, including after an add/rename/make-default action re-renders the list, and after a control becomes disabled while busy. `Esc` closes and focus returns to the `Settings` button.

## Constraints
- Any shared focus-trap helper must stay small; if the existing dialog code already provides a trap, fix the cause rather than adding a second mechanism. No new runtime dependency.
- Keep the visual language and copy unchanged. Do not restyle anything.
- Preserve the behaviours already verified: `Ctrl/Cmd+N` typing guard, unsaved-changes guard, delete confirmation copy, sample-data labelling, search, and the mobile drawer.

## Verify before handing off (tight)
1. `npm run check` and `npm test` still pass (no regressions).
2. Real browser on a fresh scratch DB and a non-default port, re-running exactly the three repros above and reporting the before/after numbers for the focus-containment sequences and the banner/Retry presence.
3. Commit early (as soon as checks pass) with `git -c user.name=DesBots -c user.email=des.agent.bot@gmail.com commit`, then write `evidence/receipts/T6-coder.md` (≤200 words: task id, candidate SHA, commands, exit codes, observed before/after, limitations) and complete the card with the SHA.
4. Do not perform a broad regression sweep — card `t_5d0de379`'s successor re-verifies the full acceptance set.

BUDGET: stop after two unsuccessful attempts at the same symptom, preserve evidence and report the blocker.

t_0270576b.title: T7 coder: apply the review's should-fix (discarded draft stays live) and reconcile the SPEC test script
t_0270576b.body:
Small fix card from the independent review (T5 reviewer receipt: `evidence/receipts/T5-reviewer.md`). Repository `/home/hermes/workspace/coffee-notes`, branch `main`, start from current HEAD (`99c1bfa`; source frozen at `c1222f9`). Use team-quality and team-verify. Keep the diff minimal — the more files this touches, the more verification it invalidates.

## F1 — should-fix: a discarded draft can still be saved (source change required)
`public/app.js`, `withGuard` (≈225-230) and `openSettings` (≈398-401). Opening Settings while the editor is dirty discards the editor in state (`state.editor = null`, `pane = 'idle'`) **without re-rendering the pane**, so the abandoned editor form stays mounted in the DOM and remains live. The reviewer's probe on a scratch instance:
`S4 editor form still in pane: 1`, `S5 placeholder: 0`, `S6 after Esc: still 1`, `S7 notes stored after saving the abandoned form: ["Stale form write", …]`, and after choosing *Discard changes* the draft is still readable and saveable (`S11`/`S12`) while `isDirty()` no longer guards it.

That contradicts two brief requirements: cancelling/discarding must not resurrect a discarded note, and unsaved edits must be protected. Every other editor exit path already re-renders; `withGuard` does not.

Reviewer's suggested smallest fix: call `renderPane()` after `closeEditor()` inside `withGuard` (mirroring the other exit paths). Verify what the real flow needs rather than assuming — the check is that after choosing *Discard changes* from the guard dialog, the discarded form is gone from the pane and cannot write to the API.

## F4 — docs drift, same card, no behaviour change
`docs/SPEC.md` §6 still documents `test: node --test test/`, but `package.json` and `scripts/check.js` use bare `node --test` because a directory argument exits 1 on Node 26.7.0 (`Cannot find module '…/test'`). Reconcile the SPEC with the working command, or note the Node-version constraint next to the script. Do not change the script itself.

## Explicitly NOT in scope (recorded as accepted nice-to-haves, do not fix here)
- Oversized bodies above ~16× the 256 KB limit drain with `req.destroy()`, giving a connection reset instead of the documented 400 (`server/router.js` ≈87-113). Server stays healthy; 300 KB still returns a clean 400.
- ~12-15 lines of unused surface: `server/api.js` re-exports `ApiError` with no importer, `server/router.js` returns `routes` unread, `public/js/drawer.js` exports `open`/`syncMode` unused, `server/static.js` exports `contentTypeFor` used only internally, `FOCUSABLE` duplicated in `dialog.js` and `drawer.js`.

## Verify before handing off (tight)
1. `npm run check` exit 0 and `npm test` 25/25 — no regressions.
2. Real browser repro on a fresh scratch DB and non-default port: load a note → `Edit` → type into a field (make it dirty) → open `Settings` → choose *Discard changes* → assert the editor form is no longer in the pane and that the discarded values cannot reach the API (the note count and the stored note are unchanged). Repeat for a **dirty new note** (the `New note` → dirty → Settings → Discard path) and assert no row is created. Report the before/after observations.
3. Confirm the normal paths still behave: dirty-edit `Cancel` reverts, clean cancel leaves the detail view, `Esc` still guards, saving a real edit still works.
4. Commit early with `git -c user.name=DesBots -c user.email=des.agent.bot@gmail.com commit`, then write `evidence/receipts/T7-coder.md` (≤200 words: task id, candidate SHA, commands, exit codes, observed before/after for both repro paths, limitations) and complete the card with the SHA.
